o.text:
Derivation from Proto-Common Turkic *it- (“to push, hit”) combined with the intensity suffix -ələ.
Cognate with Turkish itmek. Unrelated to Azerbaijani itmək.

Possibly from Proto-Turkic *ïŋïra- (“to neigh; to bellow, purr”). Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (ïŋra-), Turkish anırmak, Turkmen yňranmak (“to scream”), Chuvash ӗнер (ĕner, “to cry (of children)”), Yakut иҥэрсий (iŋersiy, “to neigh quietly”), Kazakh ыңырану (ıŋıranuw, “to moan”).
From Proto-Common Turkic *kap-gak, ultimately a derivation of Proto-Turkic *kap-. Cognate with Turkish kapak.
From ikitərəfli + simmetriyalı + -lar. Calque of Russian двусторо́нне-симметри́чные (dvustorónne-simmetríčnyje).
